Small restaurant… high quality… good prices
Aug 2025
I’m Canadian. This an honest review. I’ve eaten here 3 times so far on this trip to Danang. (August 2025)

**For the record, I’ve eaten several well-regarded sushi and omakase dinners in Tokyo.

Izakaya Yoshino Shoten is a small sushi restaurant with high quality food, good portion sizes, fair prices, clean environment, and friendly and professional staff.

I love all the tuna dishes they serve. Good portions of tuna tartar (140 VND), tuna and avocado (150 VND), seared tuna steak (180 VND), and tuna w/ avocado roll (200 VND), all of which (I believe) are using yellow-fin tuna. Blue-fin tuna was also excellent quality, with price per one sashimi piece at hakami (100 VND), chutoro (140 VND) and otoro (200 VND). If you want nigiri, just add a tiny bit to the sashimi price. Above prices are all net price in their menu. Bluefin tuna is expensive everywhere, so if you need to stick to the yellowfin tuna, don’t worry; it’s really good.

The entire menu size is not large, but they’re good at what they serve. I’d guess that most other restaurants have larger, or much larger, menus, if that’s your thing. For me, I’m mainly about the tuna. If you’re reading this, it’s because you’re looking for sushi in Danang. One well-reviewed restaurant is Sushi Be, which has a very large menu. I personally ate Sushi Be’s omakase (800 VND plus VAT) and while it was nice, in my humble opinion, I prefer Izakaya Yoshino Shoten. To be fair, in the grand scheme of things, that $33 USD omakase meal was an ok price. I just believe I get more of what I want for the same money at Izakaya Yoshino Shoten.

To Izakaya Yoshino Shoten, please continue doing what you’re doing, and please don’t start to jack your prices (or make dishes smaller) when people like your restaurant. Too many other restaurants are over-priced. Please don’t go that route. 

To readers, make sure you go to the correct location. There is another Izakaya Shoten a few steps down the same street (literally about a 20-second walk). It specializes in ramen and I heard it’s also good, but I haven’t eaten there. 

Thank you to Izakaya Yoshino Shoten for letting me enjoy some delicious tuna (and other dishes) while I’m in Danang.

Hidden gem for Japanese Restaurant in town
May 2025 • Friends
We discovered this izakaya after trying their sister restaurant in the An Thượng area, which serves some of the best ramen we’ve had. That experience set the bar high — and this place lived up to it.

The sashimi was fresh and flavorful, clearly prepared with care. Each dish looked like something out of a fine dining restaurant, with beautiful plating and attention to detail. But it wasn’t just about looks — everything tasted as good as it looked.

We also loved the open kitchen concept where you can watch the chefs in action, especially the sushi chef who not only makes great food but also adds a bit of charm to the experience (yes, he’s quite handsome!).

What really stood out is that the menu isn’t your usual run-of-the-mill Japanese selection. The flavors are well-balanced and thoughtfully crafted — you can tell they put a lot of heart into it.

The staff were friendly and welcoming, making the whole evening relaxed and enjoyable.
If you’ve tried their ramen spot and loved it, this izakaya is definitely worth checking out next.
